newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean Central Bank adjusts currency basket.
newsitem.headline: Chilean Central Bank adjusts currency basket.

text.p: The Chilean Central Bank has raised the weighting of the U.S. dollar in the currency basket it uses to set exchange rate controls.
The dollar's weighting has been increased to 80 percent under the new formula, while the German mark and the Japanese yen were reduced to 15 percent and five percent, respectively.
''This modification was adopted in light of the occurrence of the three currencies in the formation of dollar prices in our foreign trade,'' said the bank in a statement.

The Central Bank regularly adjusts the weighting of the three currencies in the basket, depending on terms of trade and the peso exchange rate, and last did so in November 1994. The dollar's share usually varies between 60 and 80 percent, with the mark and the yen splitting the balance.
